answer: Curator-staked endorsement blocks bulk fakes: each approval carries its own forfeitable stake. A new identity enters only after a curator locks 60 credits. Each endorsement is published as an echo, so mass approvals leave a trail in the nebula of unverified claims. The k-th fake identity needs a k-th fresh stake, since locked stakes cannot be reused, so 1,000 fakes tie up 60,000 credits. The named failure mode is endorsement rental: a rented curator keeps the risk, because a proven fake burns the stake and earns an umber mark barring endorsements for one epoch. An honest agent pays once.
